nodes.title: Artin v-stacks
nodes.statement: A small v-stack X is Artin when its diagonal X→X×X is representable in locally spatial diamonds and it admits a surjective separated cohomologically smooth atlas U→X with U a locally spatial diamond. Cohomological smoothness of the atlas is the supplier’s notion for separated maps representable in locally spatial diamonds, tested after every base change to a strictly totally disconnected perfectoid space. The diagonal is quasiseparated; X itself need not be quasiseparated. The property is invariant under equivalence of small v-stacks.
hypotheses: X is a small v-stack.
The diagonal X→X×X is representable in locally spatial diamonds.
There is a surjective map U→X from a locally spatial diamond that is separated and cohomologically smooth (ell-cohomologically smooth for the primes ell≠p in play).
proofSteps: Use the existing small v-stack carrier and representability, not a new category of stacks.
Store existence of an atlas as a property; compare any two atlases via U×X V and smooth descent.
Deduce quasiseparatedness of the diagonal from U×X U→U being separated; do not deduce quasiseparatedness of X.
For the classifying example use the smooth GL_n(E)-diamond quotient chart from IV.1.9(iv); the point map is not a smooth atlas for nondiscrete H.
acceptance: A locally spatial diamond with its identity atlas is Artin.
For H a locally profinite group with a closed embedding into GL_n(E), [*/H] is Artin by IV.1.9(iv). For H=E× its diagonal is not quasicompact, so the stack need not be quasiseparated.

sources.locator: Definition IV.1.1; Remarks IV.1.2–IV.1.6, pp.107–109; Example IV.1.9(iv), p.110
sources.match: Definition IV.1.1 defines an Artin v-stack by a diagonal representable in locally spatial diamonds and a surjective separated cohomologically smooth chart from a locally spatial diamond. Remarks IV.1.2–IV.1.4 deduce that the diagonal is quasiseparated and give the practical criteria; Remark IV.1.3 shows [*/G(E)] and Bun_G are not quasiseparated; Example IV.1.9(iv) treats [*/G] for G closed in GL_n(E). The node states exactly this.

nodes.title: Enhanced smooth atlas descent
nodes.statement: For an Artin v-stack X and separated smooth atlas U→X, the enhanced D_et(X,Λ), for prime-to-p torsion Λ, is equivalent to the limit of D_et(U_n,Λ) on its Čech nerve using ordinary pullbacks. It agrees with the pre-existing small-v-stack ECD category and is independent of atlas through refinement. Exceptional transition functors give the corresponding normalized smooth-lisse presentation; the enhancement and coherent limits are imported from EDS.
hypotheses: X is an Artin v-stack and U→X a separated cohomologically smooth surjection from a locally spatial diamond.
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
The enhancement of D_et and its hyperdescent are imported from EnhancedDerivedSheaves.
proofSteps: Apply enhanced hyperdescent to the Čech hypercover; use the existing coefficient category as carrier.
Compare refinements through the bisimplicial Čech nerve, retaining coherent transition maps.

Normalize exceptional transitions by the invertible smooth dualizing objects and the canonical twisted-pullback equivalence supplied by S4. Apply its ℓ-power torsion form to the finitely many primary coefficient factors of the prime-to-p annihilator, then assemble the coefficient decomposition.
acceptance: For an identity atlas the limit identifies with D_et(X,Λ).
A refinement changes neither objects nor mapping complexes.

nodes.title: Partial compact-support functors
nodes.statement: For a coefficient ring Λ killed by an integer n prime to p, over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, let X be a spatial diamond partially proper over Spd k of finite transcendence dimension, and S a spatial diamond over k. Put α:X×k S→X and β:X×k S→S. Quasi-pro-étale universally open affinoid covers and two pseudouniformizers define the annular systems U_{a,b}, U_a and U_b. Define Rβ_!+=colim_a Rβ_*j_{a!}(−|U_a) and Rβ_!-=colim_b Rβ_*j_{b!}(−|U_b), with transitions given by extension-by-zero counits. Common cofinal refinements give independence of covers and pseudouniformizers. These are partially supported functors, not an unrestricted stacky Rβ_!. No general adjunction is inferred merely from the colimit.
hypotheses: k is an algebraically closed field over F_q; everything is over Perf_k.
X is a spatial diamond with X→Spd k partially proper and dim.trg finite.
S is a spatial diamond over k.
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Choose universally open quasi-pro-étale affinoid covers of X and S; form the annular U_{a,b}, U_a, U_b by comparing the two pseudouniformizers.
Define the two systems with extension by zero and ordinary pushforward, including the direction of transition maps.
Compare parameters through cofinal annular systems; permitted base change uses the proper pushforward and colimit identities, not an arbitrary base-change assertion.
acceptance: Changing the pseudouniformizer gives cofinal systems and the same two functors.
The plus and minus functors retain their different support conditions.

proofSteps: Use a hypercover by canonical compactifications of quasi-pro-étale affinoid charts, then proper pushforward to reduce X to Spa K with K algebraically closed.

Reduce annular cones by base change and sums to the punctured-disc calculation of IV.5.1. Finite relative dimension gives the uniform bound required to commute filtered colimits with the hypercover/Postnikov limits.

nodes.title: Point maps to classifying stacks
nodes.statement: Let H be a locally profinite group admitting a closed embedding into GL_n(E), with ell≠p. If H contains an infinite compact open subgroup K, the point map *→[*/H] is not ell-cohomologically smooth: on K its exceptional dualizing sheaf is the noninvertible sheaf of F_ell-valued distributions. If H is discrete, the point map is separated étale and cohomologically smooth, including infinite discrete H. The printed finite-only exception is corrected in sourceIssues E4.
hypotheses: H is a locally profinite group with a closed embedding into GL_n(E).
ell≠p.
proofSteps: Pull back the point map along itself to obtain H→*. Restrict to a compact open subgroup K.
Use the supplier’s profinite distribution computation. For infinite K, the distribution sheaf is not invertible, obstructing smoothness.
If H is discrete, every geometric base change is a disjoint union of copies of the base, hence étale. Apply the existing étale smoothness theorem.
acceptance: For H=Z_p the point map is not a smooth atlas.
For H=π^Z⊂E× it is étale and cohomologically smooth, although H is infinite.

sources.match: Remark IV.1.10 observes that *→[*/G] pulls back to G→*, whose exceptional pullback of Λ is the sheaf of Λ-valued distributions on G, so the point is not a smooth chart; its parenthesis excepts only finite G. The node states the obstruction for groups with an infinite compact open subgroup and records that discrete G gives an étale chart (source issue E4).

nodes.title: Exceptional pullback for smooth stacky maps
nodes.statement: For a cohomologically smooth morphism f:X→Y of Artin v-stacks, define f! by descent on charts g:U→X for which g and f∘g are separated: its restriction is (f∘g)! followed by inverse smooth normalization for g. The result is f!A=ω_f⊗f*A with ω_f invertible, satisfies base change and composition on this chartwise smooth class, and agrees with the supplier on separated representable eligible maps. The stacky left adjoint exists here. This does not construct exceptional operations for all locally finite-dimensional Artin maps; Remark IV.1.14 leaves that extension unestablished.
hypotheses: f:Y→X is a cohomologically smooth map of Artin v-stacks in the sense of Convention IV.1.12: some separated smooth surjection g:V→Y from a locally spatial diamond has f∘g separated.
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p (or, where the source allows it, an adic ring in the sense of ECD §26).
proofSteps: Use charts with both required separation conditions and supplier exceptional pullbacks.
Cancel the invertible chart dualizing complexes and compare on common refinements.
Apply descent to smooth composition/base change and to the chartwise left adjoints.
acceptance: For f=id, f! is the identity and ω_f is the tensor unit.
For a smooth representable map this recovers the existing diamond exceptional inverse image.

sources.match: Definition IV.1.11 and Convention IV.1.12 define cohomologically smooth maps of Artin v-stacks through separated charts; Definition IV.1.13 gives the invertible dualizing complex with its chart compatibilities; Remark IV.1.14 warns that the compatibility is only known for separated smooth charts; Definition IV.1.15 sets Rf^!=Rf^!Λ⊗f*; Remark IV.1.16 gives the left adjoint.

nodes.title: Stability of Artin v-stacks
nodes.statement: (i) If X,Y,Z are Artin v-stacks then X×Z Y is Artin. (ii) If S→* is a pro-étale surjective, separated, cohomologically smooth map of v-sheaves representable in locally spatial diamonds, then a small v-stack X is Artin iff X×S is Artin; in particular the Artin property may be tested after base change to Spd E or to Spa F_q((t^(1/p^∞))). (iii) If f:X→Y is representable in locally spatial diamonds and Y is Artin, then X is Artin: pull back an atlas of Y and use the representable diagonal; in particular locally closed substacks of Artin v-stacks are Artin. Cohomological smoothness of maps of Artin v-stacks, defined through separated smooth charts, does not depend on the chart and is smooth-local on the source, with the separation and eligibility conditions retained.
hypotheses: All stacks are small v-stacks.
In (i) all three stacks, including the base of the fibre product, are Artin.
In (ii) S→* is pro-étale surjective, separated, cohomologically smooth and representable in locally spatial diamonds.
In (iii) the map to the Artin v-stack is representable in locally spatial diamonds.
proofSteps: Pull back the atlas of Z, then those of X and Y, obtaining a diamond atlas of the fibre product.
Express the diagonal as a fibre product of the three representable diagonals.

For (ii), compose an atlas of X×S with the projection to X, and test representability of the diagonal of X after the pro-étale surjection X×X×S→X×X, where it is the diagonal of X×S followed by a projection that is representable in locally spatial diamonds.
Use the supplier’s smooth descent for each chart comparison; representable maps use the pulled-back atlas directly.
acceptance: The middle stack Z must be Artin in the fibre-product assertion.
A representable closed or open immersion into an Artin stack has Artin source.
Part (ii) is what reduces the classifying stack [*/H] to [Spd E/H] in Example IV.1.9(iv).

sources.locator: Proposition IV.1.8; Example IV.1.9(i)–(iii); Definition IV.1.11; Convention IV.1.12, pp.109–111
sources.match: Proposition IV.1.8 proves: (i) fibre products of Artin v-stacks are Artin; (ii) for S→* pro-étale surjective, separated, cohomologically smooth and representable in locally spatial diamonds, X is Artin iff X×S is; (iii) a v-stack with a map to an Artin v-stack that is representable in locally spatial diamonds is Artin. Example IV.1.9(i)–(iii) draws the consequences for base points and locally closed substacks. Definition IV.1.11 with Convention IV.1.12 makes smoothness of maps of Artin v-stacks chart-independent.

nodes.title: Braden’s theorem for diamonds
nodes.statement: In the preceding proper finite-dimensional setup, for every A∈D_et(X/G_m,Λ), pulled back to X, the canonical map L−A→L+A is an equivalence; hence it is an equivalence for every monodromic A. More precisely, for A⁺∈D_et(X⁺/G_m,Λ) the map R(i⁺)!A⁺→R(p⁺)_!A⁺, and for A⁻∈D_et(X⁻/G_m,Λ) the map R(p⁻)_*A⁻→(i⁻)*A⁻, are equivalences, so that L−A≃(i⁻)*R(q⁻)!A≃R(i⁺)!(q⁺)*A≃L+A. For the more general compactifiable local setup of IV.6.9 the source requires bounded-below A, unless finite relative dimension is imposed. The global finite-dimensional theorem has no additional bounded-below restriction.
hypotheses: S is a small v-stack and f:X→S is proper, representable in spatial diamonds, with dim.trg finite, and carries a G_m-action satisfying Hypothesis IV.6.1.
A comes from D_et(X/G_m,Λ), or is monodromic in the sense of Definition IV.6.11.
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: First prove contraction for equivariant objects by IV.5 vanishing on the punctured attracting/repelling pieces.
Use the local closed fixed-point square and the quotient qcqs/flow hypotheses to establish the comparison, with the correct boundedness in IV.6.9.
Pass to finite colimits and retracts to obtain the monodromic theorem.
acceptance: The comparison is the identity for a trivial action.
Forgetting monodromicity is not authorized by the theorem.

sources.locator: Theorem IV.6.5; Proposition IV.6.6; Remark IV.6.7; Lemma IV.6.8; Proposition IV.6.9; Lemma IV.6.10, pp.158–162
sources.match: Theorem IV.6.5 states that L−A→L+A is an isomorphism for A pulled back from D_et(X/G_m,Λ), together with the two contraction isomorphisms R(i+)^!A+≅R(p+)_!A+ and R(p−)_*A−≅(i−)^*A− for equivariant A±. Proposition IV.6.6 is the vanishing of one-ended partially supported cohomology for G_m-equivariant sheaves, reduced to Theorem IV.5.3; Lemma IV.6.8 gives the qcqs quotients; Proposition IV.6.9 with Lemma IV.6.10 is the local comparison, for bounded-below A or all A when dim.trg is finite.

nodes.title: The divisor-to-Weil classifying map
nodes.statement: For a nonarchimedean local field E with residue F_q, work over k=algebraic closure of F_q. With C a completed algebraic closure of E, Div¹≃Spd Ĕ/φ^Z≃[Spd C/W_E], where τ acts on Spd C as τ∘Frob^(−deg τ). Define ψ:Div¹→[*/W_E] by this torsor quotient, and ψ_X^I:X×(Div¹)^I→X×[*/W_E^I]. The Weil group, its degree and Weil topology are imported from ClassFieldTheory layer 9; the divisor space is imported from RelativeFarguesFontaine.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q; k is the algebraic closure of F_q; everything is over Perf_k.
W_E is the Weil group of E with its Weil topology and degree map, imported from the Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory roadmap.
Div¹ and its presentation are imported from RelativeFarguesFontaine.
proofSteps: Use the supplied degree map to twist the Galois action so that both Frobenii cancel on Spd k.
Identify the torsor relation W_E×Spd C≃Spd C×Div¹ Spd C and the quotient.
Take the classifying map and finite products; do not construct the Weil group again.
acceptance: Inertia acts by the usual Galois action because its degree is zero.
The topology is the Weil topology, with its fixed profinite inertia open, rather than the subspace topology from G_E.

sources.locator: IV.7, construction before Proposition IV.7.1, p.164
sources.match: The opening of IV.7 writes Div¹=Spd Ĕ/φ^Z over Perf_k with k the algebraic closure of F_q, lets W_E act on Spd C for C the completed algebraic closure of E by τ∘Frob^(−deg τ), identifies [Spd C/W_E] with [Spd Ĕ/φ^Z], and so defines ψ:Div¹→[*/W_E] and ψ_X for every small v-stack X.

nodes.title: Drinfeld’s lemma for perfect local systems
nodes.statement: For every finite I, small v-stack X, and prime-to-p torsion Λ, ψ_X^I* gives D_lc(X×[*/W_E^I],Λ)≃D_lc(X×(Div¹)^I,Λ). This is the locally constant perfect formulation, not an unrestricted assertion π1((Div¹)^I)=W_E^I for a conventional profinite fundamental group.
hypotheses: I is a finite set and X a small v-stack over k (the algebraic closure of F_q).
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Use full faithfulness and induction on I; v-descent reduces X to strict-local rank-one points.
Reduce coefficients to a discrete completed regular F_ell-algebra and perfect complexes to finite modules; finite étale covers trivialize the reductions.

Use the inertia-surjective Gauss point of FS II.1.14 to force the completed action to be discrete on an open inertia subgroup, then descend the isomorphism to a finite extension and the small étale site.
acceptance: For I empty the equivalence is identity.
Partial-diagonal supported objects show that replacing D_lc by all D_et is false.

sources.match: Proposition IV.7.3 states that pullback D_lc(X×[*/W_E^I],Λ)→D_lc(X×(Div¹)^I,Λ) is an equivalence for every finite I and small v-stack X, and remarks that it fails without local constancy because of sheaves supported on partial diagonals. Its proof reduces to a geometric rank-one point and a complete regular local F_ell-algebra, trivialises the reductions by SW20 Lemma 16.3.2, and uses the point of Lemma II.1.14 with inertia-surjective Galois group to make the limit action discrete.

nodes.title: Fully faithful divisor descent
nodes.statement: For every small v-stack X and prime-to-p torsion Λ, ψ_X* is fully faithful on D_et. It is an equivalence if D_et(X,Λ)→D_et(X×Spd C,Λ) is an equivalence. For every finite I, ψ_X^I* remains fully faithful. Essential surjectivity of the full category is conditional; this is not a general product formula for fundamental groups.
hypotheses: X is a small v-stack over k; I is a finite set.
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Compare the Cartesian categories on X×W_E^• and X×Spd C×W_E^• via ECD algebraically closed base-change full faithfulness.
Degree-zero essential surjectivity suffices for Cartesian descent when the stated base-change equivalence holds.
Induct on the finite set of divisor factors.
acceptance: The empty-index case is the identity.
Sheaves on proper partial diagonals show why full D_et essential surjectivity is not automatic.

sources.match: Proposition IV.7.1 states that ψ_X* is fully faithful on D_et and an equivalence when D_et(X,Λ)→D_et(X×Spd C,Λ) is one; the proof is descent along *→[*/W_E] and ECD Theorem 1.13 (invariance under change of algebraically closed base). Corollary IV.7.2 is the fully faithful version for finite I.

nodes.title: Formal smoothness of v-stacks
nodes.statement: A map X→Y is formally smooth in the IV.3 sense if for every characteristic-p affinoid perfectoid S, Zariski closed subspace S0⊂S, map S→Y and compatible S0→X, there are an étale map S′→S whose image contains all of |S0| and a lift S′→X over Y agreeing with the prescribed map after pullback to S′×S S0. This is lifting along Zariski closed subspaces of affinoid perfectoid spaces, not along nilpotent thickenings of schemes.
hypotheses: f is a map of v-stacks.
Test objects: S affinoid perfectoid of characteristic p, S_0⊂S Zariski closed, with compatible maps S_0→source and S→target.
proofSteps: Use Zariski closed embeddings of affinoid perfectoid spaces and étale neighbourhoods.
Define the lifting property by all such squares with the prescribed restriction on S0.
Store it as a property of the actual stack morphism; formal smoothness is not replaced by an unspecified predicate.
acceptance: Étale maps satisfy the lifting condition locally.
This condition gives the openness and local sections used in the Jacobian proof.

sources.match: Definition IV.3.1 defines a map f:Y→X of v-stacks to be formally smooth when every square from a Zariski closed subspace S_0⊂S of a characteristic-p affinoid perfectoid space admits, on an étale S′→S whose image contains S_0, a lift agreeing with the given map on S′×_S S_0.

nodes.title: Formal smoothness and local sections
nodes.statement: Formal smoothness of small v-stack maps is stable under composition and base change and gives universal openness. For maps of locally spatial diamonds it is étale-local on both sides. A formally smooth v-surjection of small v-stacks admits étale-local sections. Corollary IV.3.6 is the descent statement through a formally smooth surjection; no descent through an arbitrary map is asserted.
hypotheses: The maps are maps of v-stacks; locality on source and target is asserted only for maps of locally spatial diamonds.
Sections exist étale-locally only for formally smooth maps that are surjective.
proofSteps: Compose lift problems and pull them back to prove the formal identities.

Embed a test object as a Zariski closed subspace of a perfectoid ball over the base, extend the map to an étale neighbourhood by formal smoothness, descend that neighbourhood to a finite-dimensional ball by the source’s approximation, and use that cohomologically smooth maps are open.
Apply the lifting property to a v-local section and descend through an étale neighbourhood, preserving the given closed lift.
acceptance: The section conclusion uses v-surjectivity in addition to formal smoothness.
The statement uses characteristic-p perfectoid lift tests, not infinitesimal scheme smoothness.

sources.locator: Observations (i)–(iv) following Definition IV.3.1; Propositions IV.3.2 and IV.3.5; Corollary IV.3.6, pp.131–132
sources.match: The observations (i)–(iv) after Definition IV.3.1 give stability under composition and pullback, formal smoothness of étale maps and étale locality for maps of locally spatial diamonds. Proposition IV.3.2 proves universal openness by embedding into a ball and approximating an étale neighbourhood at a finite stage; Proposition IV.3.5 gives étale-local sections of formally smooth surjections; Corollary IV.3.6 is descent of formal smoothness through a formally smooth v-surjection.

nodes.title: Formally smooth diamonds and Banach–Colmez spaces
nodes.statement: On perfectoid spaces of characteristic p, the v-sheaves B=O⁺ and A¹=O are formally smooth over the point, and so is Spd O_E for a nonarchimedean local field E. If f:Y→X is a smooth morphism of analytic adic spaces over Z_p, then the associated map of diamonds is formally smooth. For a perfectoid space S and a map [E₁→E₀] of vector bundles on X_S with E₀ everywhere of positive and E₁ everywhere of negative Harder–Narasimhan slopes, BC([E₁→E₀])→S is formally smooth.
hypotheses: In IV.3.3 the base is the point, on perfectoid spaces of characteristic p; E is a nonarchimedean local field.
In IV.3.4, f is a smooth morphism of analytic adic spaces over Z_p.
In IV.3.8, S is a perfectoid space and [E_1→E_0] a map of vector bundles on X_S with E_0 everywhere of positive and E_1 everywhere of negative Harder–Narasimhan slopes.
proofSteps: For a Zariski closed immersion of affinoid perfectoid spaces the map on functions R→R₀ is surjective, which lifts points of A¹; B is open in A¹. For Spd O_E, write an untilt of S₀ by a primitive element π+Σπ^i[r_i] with topologically nilpotent r_i, and lift the r_i along the surjection on topologically nilpotent elements.
A smooth map of analytic adic spaces is locally étale over a finite-dimensional ball; combine the ball case with formal smoothness of étale maps and étale locality on source and target.

Use the exact sequence 0→BC(E₀)→BC([E₁→E₀])→BC(E₁[1])→0 and étale-local surjectivity of its second map to reduce to the two outer terms. For E₀, choose étale locally a surjection from a sum of copies of O(1/r) with kernel of positive slopes and vanishing H¹ over affinoid perfectoid test objects, which reduces to the perfectoid open unit disc. For E₁, embed it in a sum of copies of O(d) with positive-slope cokernel G; then BC(G)→BC(E₁[1]) is a formally smooth surjection from a formally smooth source, and descent of formal smoothness through a formally smooth surjection finishes.
acceptance: For E₁=0 and E₀=O(1/r) the space is a perfectoid open unit disc over S, formally smooth by the ball case.
The lift for Spd O_E is an untilt over O_E, which may have characteristic p on part of the test object: the special fibre is included.
The proof of the Jacobian criterion uses the Banach–Colmez case in its presentation of projectivized Banach–Colmez spaces (FS Lemma IV.4.28).

sources.locator: Propositions IV.3.3 and IV.3.8; Corollary IV.3.4, pp.131–133; used in the proof of Lemma IV.4.28, pp.147–148
sources.match: Proposition IV.3.3 proves that B=O⁺, A¹=O and Spd O_E are formally smooth over the point, using surjectivity of R→R_0 and of R°°→R_0°° for a Zariski closed immersion; Corollary IV.3.4 deduces formal smoothness of the diamond of a smooth map of analytic adic spaces over Z_p; Proposition IV.3.8 proves formal smoothness of BC([E_1→E_0])→S when E_0 has positive and E_1 negative slopes, by reduction to perfectoid open unit discs and Corollary IV.3.6. The proof of Lemma IV.4.28, inside the proof of the Jacobian criterion, cites IV.3.8.

nodes.title: Geometric finite étale descent for divisors
nodes.statement: For E a nonarchimedean local field and C0 an algebraically closed characteristic-p perfectoid field over k, finite étale covers of Spa C0×Div¹ come by pullback from Div¹. The geometric curve input is the exact supplier theorem that every finite étale O_X-algebra on the absolute Fargues–Fontaine curve over an algebraically closed point equals O_X⊗E A with A finite étale over E. In SW20 the displayed field is Q_p; the proof works in this E-generality using the supplied E-bundle classification and finite étale adic/diamond comparison.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field; C_0 is an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field of characteristic p over k.
The printed lemma is for E=Q_p; the E-generality rests on the supplier's finite étale theorem for the curve of E.
proofSteps: Identify the finite étale curve/diamond sites by the supplied comparison and Frobenius relocation.
Import, rather than re-prove, the finite étale algebra theorem from VB2; it reduces covers to finite étale E-algebras.

Use the curve/diamond comparison, Frobenius relocation and the imported constant finite-étale E-algebra classification to obtain the pullback equivalence for covers of Spa C0×Div¹. This is Lemma 16.3.2, not the connected-fibre product theorem 16.3.3.
acceptance: For E=Q_p this recovers SW20 Lemma 16.3.2 exactly.
The algebra A need not be E: finite arithmetic covers remain; geometric simple connectedness does not mean no arithmetic covers.

sources.locator: Lemma 16.3.2 and the paragraph after it, p.144; Theorem 13.5.7, p.114
sources.match: Lemma 16.3.2 states that for C algebraically closed nonarchimedean over F_p, the fundamental group of (Spd Q_p/Frobenius)×Spd C is the absolute Galois group of Q_p; the text deduces it from the comparison of the finite étale sites of the Fargues–Fontaine curve and of its diamond and from Theorem 13.5.7, which says every finite étale cover of the curve comes from a finite étale Q_p-algebra.
The proof of Proposition IV.7.3 uses the lemma in the form: every finite étale cover of Spa C×Div¹ is pulled back from Div¹, for the local field E.

nodes.title: Hyperbolic base change, duality and ULA
nodes.statement: For the proper finite-dimensional hyperbolic setup and monodromic objects, L commutes with base pullback and ordinary base pushforward. It commutes with supported pushforward and exceptional base pullback when the base map is compactifiable representable locally spatial of finite relative dimension. Relative Verdier duality exchanges L for an action with L for the inverse action. If A is f-ULA, LA is f0-ULA.
hypotheses: The setup of Definition IV.6.11: f:X→S proper, representable in spatial diamonds, dim.trg finite, with a G_m-action satisfying Hypothesis IV.6.1.
A is monodromic.
For the two exceptional commutations the base change is compactifiable, representable in locally spatial diamonds, with dim.trg finite.
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Use L+ for star base change and supported pushforward, and L− for ordinary pushforward and exceptional pullback.
Apply tensor-Hom adjunction to Rp+!q+*; its relative dual is the inverse-action L−.
Prove the two ULA clauses after base change using the finite-dimensional proper fixed-point setup and the source’s local contraction argument.
acceptance: Verdier duality reverses the action; it does not simply preserve the chosen plus correspondence.
The eligibility restriction is retained for the two exceptional base-change identities.

sources.match: Proposition IV.6.12 gives the four commutations of hyperbolic localization with pullback, pushforward, supported pushforward and exceptional pullback along a base change (the last two for compactifiable representable maps of finite dim.trg); Proposition IV.6.13 exchanges it with relative Verdier duality up to inverting the action; Proposition IV.6.14 shows it preserves ULA.

nodes.title: Hyperbolic localization and monodromic sheaves
nodes.statement: Let f:X→S be proper representable in spatial diamonds of finite relative transcendence dimension, with a G_m-action satisfying Hypothesis IV.6.1: finitely many open-and-closed fixed pieces X_i^0 and locally closed attracting/repelling X_i^± covering X, with action extensions to (A¹)^±. Set X^±=disjoint union X_i^±, q±:X±→X and p±:X±→X0. Equivariant maps (A¹)^±→X intrinsically represent these spaces, independent of the decomposition. Define L+=Rp+!q+* and L−=Rp−*q−!, with the natural comparison L−→L+. The monodromic subcategory is generated under finite colimits and retracts by pullbacks from D_et(X/G_m,Λ).
hypotheses: S is a small v-stack; f:X→S is proper, representable in spatial diamonds, with dim.trg finite.
X/S carries a G_m-action satisfying Hypothesis IV.6.1.
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Construct fixed, attracting and repelling subfunctors using the source action extensions; evaluate at 0 and 1.
The intrinsic equivariant-map characterization compares different decompositions and gives representability.
Use the Cartesian fixed-point square, base change and adjunction units/counits to construct L−→L+; close the equivariant image under the prescribed finite operations.
acceptance: The definitions distinguish q−! from q−*, and p+! from p+*.
Monodromic here is a thick subcategory, not arbitrary sheaves or closure under all sums by definition.

sources.locator: Hypothesis IV.6.1; Proposition IV.6.2; Lemma IV.6.3; Definition IV.6.4; Definition IV.6.11, pp.155–157,162
sources.match: Hypothesis IV.6.1 is the decomposition of the fixed locus with attracting and repelling pieces to which the action extends; Proposition IV.6.2 identifies X± with G_m-equivariant maps from (A¹)± and so shows independence of the decomposition; Lemma IV.6.3 identifies X⁰ with an open and closed part of X⁺×_X X⁻; Definition IV.6.4 defines L+=R(p+)_!(q+)^*, L−=R(p−)_*R(q−)^! and the map L−→L+; Definition IV.6.11 defines monodromic sheaves and the functor L on them.

nodes.title: Jacobian criterion for cohomological smoothness
nodes.statement: Under the preceding smooth/quasiprojective section hypotheses, M_Z is a locally spatial diamond, compactifiable over S, and M_Z^sm is an open subfunctor cohomologically smooth over S. At a geometric section its ell-dimension is deg(s*T_Z/X_S), locally finite. No global dimension bound is assumed. Strictly positive slopes are essential to this criterion.
hypotheses: S is a perfectoid space over F_q.
Z→X_S is a smooth map of sous-perfectoid adic spaces.
Z admits a Zariski closed immersion into an open subset of the adic projective space P^n over X_S for some n.
ell≠p.
proofSteps: Locally on S, use the Zariski closed immersion of Z into an open subset of projective space supplied by the section-space node, and its relative normal-cone deformation; do not infer the theorem from arbitrary local embeddings on Z.

Construct section lifts by successive Frobenius corrections with positive-slope estimates, which gives formal smoothness of the smooth locus. Cover the section space by charts that are formally smooth and Zariski closed in spaces étale over a perfectoid ball, using the presentation of projectivized Banach–Colmez spaces and their formal smoothness; étale retractions then give constant-sheaf ULA.
Deform the section to its normal/tangent cone, use ULA and constructibility to stabilize the family, and identify the dualizing fibre with that of the positive BC tangent space.
acceptance: For V=O(1), the criterion recovers the supplied BC smoothness and degree dimension.
The Quot inequality max slope(ker)<min slope(F) gives its smooth section locus.

sources.locator: Theorem IV.4.2, p.134; Propositions IV.4.21–IV.4.22, IV.4.24, IV.4.27, IV.4.29 with Lemmas IV.4.23, IV.4.25–IV.4.26, IV.4.28, IV.4.30, pp.141–151

The proof is: Propositions IV.4.21–IV.4.22 (representability and compactifiability, with Lemma IV.4.23), Proposition IV.4.24 (formal smoothness, with Lemmas IV.4.25–IV.4.26), Proposition IV.4.27 (the constant sheaf is ULA, with Lemma IV.4.28), Proposition IV.4.29 (invertibility of the dualizing complex by deformation to the normal cone, with Lemma IV.4.30).

nodes.title: The category of cohomological kernels
nodes.statement: For Λ killed by an integer prime to p, for a small v-stack S, C_S has objects compactifiable representable locally spatial X→S of locally finite transcendence dimension, Hom(X,Y)=D_et(X×S Y,Λ), composition A⋆B=Rπ13!(π12*A⊗π23*B), and identity Δ!Λ. The eligible operations give the associator and units in this 2-category. Relative Verdier duality is D_X/S(A)=RHom(A,Rf!Λ). This is the kernel 2-category used for ULA adjoints, not ordinary rigidity of a monoidal category.
hypotheses: S is a small v-stack.
Objects are maps X→S that are compactifiable, representable in locally spatial diamonds, with locally finite dim.trg.
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Construct the Hom categories from existing coefficient categories, not new arbitrary types.
Use base change and projection to identify the two triple-convolution composites.
Use diagonal adjunction for units and transposition for C_S≃C_S^op.
acceptance: The identity kernel is Δ!Λ, not the constant sheaf on X×S X.
Kernel adjunction includes units/counits satisfying both triangle identities.

sources.locator: IV.2.3.3, construction before Theorem IV.2.23, p.124

nodes.title: Perfect locally constant complexes
nodes.statement: D_lc(Y,Λ) is the full subcategory of D_et(Y,Λ) whose objects are v-locally constant with perfect derived Λ-fibres. These are exactly tensor-dualizable objects; on spatial diamonds they are étale-locally constant. The word perfect describes the full complex, including bounded Tor amplitude, and is stronger than finite-dimensional cohomology in each degree.
hypotheses: Y is a small v-stack.
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Define the full subcategory by local trivializations with actual perfect Λ-complexes.
Dualizable objects descend v-locally; geometric-point dualizability identifies perfect fibres.
Smooth/étale locality on spatial diamonds upgrades these trivializations as in IV.2.6.
acceptance: At a geometric point this is Perf(Λ), not all D(Λ).
This D_lc is distinct from the localizing D_lis of VS3.

nodes.title: Perfect internal Hom and local acyclicity
nodes.statement: For a spatial diamond X, perfect-constructible A and any small-v-stack map g:Y→X, g*RHom(A,B)→RHom(g*A,g*B) is an isomorphism for all B, and RHom(A,Λ) is overconvergent. For an eligible f:X→S and f-ULA A, the formation of RHom(A,f!B), and in particular of the relative Verdier dual D_X/S(A), commutes with every base change S′→S of locally spatial diamonds. For such A, D_X/S(A)⊗f*B≃RHom(A,f!B). Conversely this formula, together with overconvergence, characterizes LA under the local uniform bound on the cohomological dimension of separated qc étale neighborhoods of X. Universally on S it characterizes ULA with overconvergence retained. Affinoid perfectoid maps to spatial S admit the cofinal relative-ball neighborhoods of IV.2.16 used to prove the formula.
hypotheses: f:X→S is a compactifiable map of locally spatial diamonds with locally finite dim.trg.
In IV.2.17–IV.2.18, X is spatial and A perfect-constructible.
In IV.2.15 and IV.2.19, A is f-universally locally acyclic.
In Remark IV.2.21(i), locally on X the étale cohomological dimension of quasicompact separated étale U→X is uniformly bounded.
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Use the relative affinoid-ball approximation and smooth base change to compute perfect-constructible Hom on geometric stalks.

After arbitrary base change, ULA, duality and the rank-one specialization triangle prove overconvergence and the tensor-Hom formula of IV.2.19. The non-universal converse retains the separate IV.2.21 dimension bound.
For the converse, adjunction and Neeman’s compactness lemma give perfect constructibility; the stated uniform dimension bound makes section functors commute with sums.
acceptance: The Hom comparison requires A perfect-constructible, not arbitrary A.
Overconvergence cannot be removed from the converse.

sources.locator: Proposition IV.2.15; Lemmas IV.2.16–IV.2.18; Proposition IV.2.19; Lemma IV.2.20; Remark IV.2.21, pp.119–123
sources.match: Proposition IV.2.15 proves that for f-ULA A the formation of RHom(A,Rf^!B) commutes with base change in S; Lemma IV.2.16 writes an affinoid perfectoid space over a spatial diamond as a cofiltered limit of quasicompact opens in finite-dimensional balls; Lemma IV.2.17 gives base change for RHom out of a perfect-constructible complex; Lemma IV.2.18 shows its naive dual is overconvergent; Proposition IV.2.19 is the isomorphism D_{X/S}(A)⊗f*B≅RHom(A,Rf^!B) for f-ULA A; Lemma IV.2.20 is Neeman's criterion; Remark IV.2.21 gives the converse characterisations, with the uniform bound on cohomological dimension in the non-universal case.

nodes.title: Relative section spaces and positive tangent locus
nodes.statement: For a perfectoid S/F_q and smooth Z→X_S over the relative Fargues–Fontaine curve, assume, locally on S, a Zariski closed immersion (FS Definition IV.4.20) of Z into an open subset of the adic projective space Pⁿ over X_S; the source assumes it globally, and its conclusions are local on S. Define M_Z(T)=sections X_T→Z_T. Its open subfunctor M_Z^sm consists of sections s for which s*T_Z/X_S has only strictly positive slopes at every geometric point. The source uses the candidate tangent/obstruction cohomology RΓ(X_T,s*T_Z/X_S): positive slopes kill H¹ and H⁰ is the supplied positive Banach–Colmez space. Its normal-cone construction identifies the zero-section fibre with BC(s*T_Z/X_S); it does not directly identify an infinitesimal deformation theory of M_Z. Smoothness and differentials on sousperfectoid charts are imported from AdicSpacesPartII.
hypotheses: S is a perfectoid space over F_q.
Z→X_S is a smooth map of sous-perfectoid adic spaces.
Locally on S, Z admits a Zariski closed immersion into an open subset of the adic projective space over X_S.
proofSteps: Sheafify relative sections by the supplied bundle/curve descent and identify pullback maps.
Define positivity through geometric HN slopes, not by a free boolean label.
Use the normal-cone deformation and its zero-section fibre BC(s*T_Z/X_S) in IV.4; the quantitative lifting estimates needed for the Jacobian criterion remain recorded in G-jacobian.
acceptance: For Z=X_S, the unique section has zero tangent and lies in M_Z^sm.
For Z the vector bundle V, the section functor is BC(V), and all sections lie in the smooth locus if V has strictly positive slopes.

sources.locator: IV.4 preamble, p.133–134; Definition IV.4.1; Theorem IV.4.2; Remark IV.4.6; Example IV.4.7, pp.134–135; Definition IV.4.20, p.141
sources.match: The opening of IV.4 defines M_Z as the v-sheaf of sections of a smooth map Z→X_S of sous-perfectoid spaces and explains the expected tangent and obstruction spaces H⁰ and H¹ of s*T_{Z/X_S}; Definition IV.4.1 defines the open subfunctor M_Z^sm by positivity of all slopes of s*T; the text after it says no direct infinitesimal relation to BC(s*T) is proved and that a deformation to the normal cone replaces it; Remark IV.4.6 shows a Zariski closed immersion into an open of P(E) is equivalent, locally on S, to one into an open of P^n; Example IV.4.7 is the Quot diamond; Definition IV.4.20 defines Zariski closed immersions of smooth sous-perfectoid spaces.

nodes.title: Cohomological smoothness of Spd O_E
nodes.statement: For a nonarchimedean local field E with residue F_q and ell≠p, Spd O_E→Spd F_q is ell-cohomologically smooth, and its dualizing object is F_ell(1)[2]. The integral special fibre is included; smoothness of the generic fibre alone does not establish this.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q.
ell≠p.
proofSteps: In equal characteristic use the perfectoid formal disc. In mixed characteristic choose a totally ramified Z_p-extension and descend constructibility by exact pro-p invariants, as in the proof of ECD 24.3.
Apply the smoothness criterion after proving the constant sheaf is ULA.
For j:Spd E→Spd O_E and its closed special fibre i, use transitivity i!f!F_ell=F_ell and j*f!F_ell=F_ell(1)[2]. The localization triangle and the local Kummer calculation give f!F_ell=F_ell(1)[2].
acceptance: The dualizing shift is [2].
The closed fibre is not removed from the conclusion.

sources.match: Corollary IV.2.34 states that Spd O_E→Spd F_q is ell-cohomologically smooth for all ell≠p. Its proof shows the constant sheaf is ULA by passing to a totally ramified Z_p-extension, where the base is a perfectoid formal disc, and then computes Rf^!F_ell≅F_ell(1)[2] from the triangle of the open generic and closed special fibres.

nodes.title: Smoothness and duality criteria
nodes.statement: For smooth f:X→S of Artin v-stacks, A is ULA iff p1*RHom(A,Λ)⊗p2*A→RHom(p1*A,p2*A) is an equivalence. For a compactifiable representable diamond map of locally finite dimension, f is ell-cohomologically smooth iff F_ell is f-ULA and Rf!F_ell is invertible.
hypotheses: In IV.2.32, f:X→S is a cohomologically smooth map of Artin v-stacks and A∈D_et(X,Λ).
In IV.2.33, f is a compactifiable map of v-stacks, representable in locally spatial diamonds, with locally finite dim.trg; ell≠p.
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Descend the kernel criterion to charts; smooth invertible dualizing objects cancel from both sides.
Use ULA exceptional base change and invertibility to recover the supplier’s smoothness characterization.
acceptance: The criterion descends through actual smooth charts.
Invertibility is necessary in addition to constant-sheaf ULA.

sources.match: Proposition IV.2.32 characterises ULA for a cohomologically smooth map of Artin v-stacks by the isomorphism p_1^*RHom(A,Λ)⊗p_2^*A→RHom(p_1^*A,p_2^*A); Proposition IV.2.33 characterises ell-cohomological smoothness of a compactifiable representable map with locally finite dim.trg by: F_ell is f-ULA and Rf^!F_ell is invertible.

nodes.title: ULA and analytification
nodes.statement: For a complete nonarchimedean field K of residue characteristic p, separated locally finite-type K-scheme map f:X→S and A∈D_c^b(X,Λ), algebraic f-ULA is equivalent to diamond ULA of the analytification A_ad for f_ad,diamond. The bounded constructible range and all prime-to-p coefficient assumptions are retained.
hypotheses: K is a complete nonarchimedean field with residue characteristic p.
f:X→S is a separated morphism of K-schemes locally of finite type.
A∈D^b_c(X,Λ).
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Import the algebraic Lu–Zheng dualizability criterion and the scheme/analytic comparison of operations.
In particular import the open-immersion Rj* comparison; tensor, pullback, ! and internal Hom then transport the dualizability map.
Apply the diamond criterion in both directions.
acceptance: For S=Spec K all bounded constructible complexes produce ULA analytifications.
This comparison is a VS1 need; it is not a prerequisite of D_lis in VS3.

sources.match: Proposition IV.2.30 states that for a separated morphism f of K-schemes locally of finite type and A in D^b_c, A is f-universally locally acyclic iff its analytification is ULA for the map of diamonds; the proof transports the criterion of Theorem IV.2.23(ii), valid algebraically by Lu–Zheng, and footnote 2 reduces the compatibility of operations to Huber's theorem for Rj_* of an open immersion.

nodes.title: Local acyclicity and universal local acyclicity
nodes.statement: For a compactifiable f:X→S of locally spatial diamonds with locally finite transcendence dimension and nΛ=0, (n,p)=1, A∈D_et(X,Λ) is locally acyclic if (a) for every geometric x over s and generization t of s, RΓ(X_x,A)→RΓ(X_x×S_s S_t,A) is an equivalence, and (b) for every separated étale j:U→X with f∘j quasicompact, R(f∘j)_!(A|U) is perfect-constructible. It is ULA if both conditions hold after every locally spatial base change S′→S. Strict localizations and perfect-constructibility are the supplied geometric notions. For a compactifiable map f:X→S of small v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally finite transcendence dimension, A is f-ULA if for every map S′→S from a locally spatial diamond the pullback of A to X×S S′ is locally acyclic for the base change of f.
hypotheses: f:X→S is a compactifiable map of locally spatial diamonds with locally finite dim.trg; in the extension, a compactifiable map of small v-stacks representable in locally spatial diamonds with locally finite dim.trg.
A∈D_et(X,Λ).
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Use actual strict-local stalk comparison maps for (a), including higher-rank geometric points.
Test compactly supported direct images on the separated étale basis for (b).
Quantify the conjunction over all base changes; étale descent of perfect-constructibility gives independence of the chosen basis.
acceptance: Over a geometric point ULA includes perfection/constructibility, not just stalk constancy.
Both clauses persist in the universal definition.

sources.locator: Definition IV.2.1; Remarks IV.2.2–IV.2.3, pp.114–115; Definition IV.2.22, p.123
sources.match: Definition IV.2.1 defines f-local acyclicity by (a) the specialisation isomorphism on strict localisations and (b) perfect-constructibility of R(f∘j)_!(A|_U) for separated étale j with f∘j quasicompact, and universal local acyclicity by requiring both after every base change of locally spatial diamonds; Remarks IV.2.2–IV.2.3 reformulate (a) as relative overconvergence. Definition IV.2.22 extends the notion to a base that is a small v-stack.

nodes.title: ULA locality and proper pushforward
nodes.statement: Clause (a) of local acyclicity holds after every base change iff A is overconvergent. Local acyclicity descends along v-covers of the base. On a spatial diamond a constructible sheaf is locally constant iff it is overconvergent, and a perfect-constructible complex is overconvergent iff it is locally a constant perfect complex; hence for f the identity, A is locally acyclic iff it is locally constant with perfect fibres. For separated f that is ell-cohomologically smooth for every ell dividing n, locally constant complexes with perfect fibres are f-ULA. For a proper map g:Y→X and compactifiable f:X→S, both of locally finite transcendence dimension, Rg_* carries complexes that are LA (respectively ULA) for f∘g to complexes that are LA (respectively ULA) for f; in particular for proper f, Rf_* of an f-LA complex is locally a constant perfect complex. For a separated map g:Y→X that is ell-cohomologically smooth for every ell dividing n, g* preserves LA and ULA, and detects them when g is surjective. The non-universal local acyclicity statements for smooth g assume that S is spatial with a uniform bound on the étale cohomological dimension of quasicompact separated étale U→S; the ULA statements require no extra uniform bound on the base.
hypotheses: f:X→S is a compactifiable map of locally spatial diamonds with locally finite dim.trg.
In IV.2.11, g:Y→X is proper with dim.trg finite; in IV.2.13, g is separated and ell-cohomologically smooth for every ell dividing n, and surjective for the converse.
The non-universal statements of IV.2.13 assume S spatial with a uniform bound on the étale cohomological dimension of quasicompact separated étale U→S.
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Descent of clause (a) is stalkwise; proper base change and perfect-constructible descent prove clause (b). Universal clause (a) is tested on the base change along a strict localization, which gives overconvergence.

Constructible sheaves on a strict localization are the 2-colimit over étale neighbourhoods, where locally constant, constant and overconvergent coincide; this gives the spatial-diamond statements and the case of the identity.
For smooth source descent use projection formulas and the smooth dualizing object; reduce universal assertions to strictly totally disconnected base changes.
For proper representable g of locally finite relative dimension, proper base change and preservation of perfect constructibility prove the direct-image ULA clauses universally over the base.
acceptance: A smooth cover detects ULA, but an arbitrary surjective map of sources is not substituted.
The statement does not silently transfer the cohomological-dimension hypothesis of the LA proof to the ULA definition.

sources.locator: Propositions IV.2.4–IV.2.6, IV.2.9–IV.2.11, IV.2.13; Corollary IV.2.12; Lemma IV.2.14, pp.115–119
sources.match: Proposition IV.2.4: clause (a) holds universally iff A is overconvergent. Proposition IV.2.5: local acyclicity descends along v-covers of the base. Proposition IV.2.6: on a spatial diamond, constructible and overconvergent means locally constant, and likewise for perfect-constructible complexes. Proposition IV.2.9: for the identity, locally acyclic means locally constant with perfect fibres. Proposition IV.2.10: for separated smooth f, locally constant complexes with perfect fibres are ULA. Proposition IV.2.11 and Corollary IV.2.12: proper pushforward preserves (U)LA. Proposition IV.2.13 with Lemma IV.2.14: (U)LA is local for separated cohomologically smooth maps of the source.

nodes.title: ULA as a kernel adjoint
nodes.statement: For X→S in C_S and A∈D_et(X,Λ), A is ULA iff p1*D_X/S(A)⊗p2*A→RHom(p1*A,p2!A) is an equivalence, iff A∈Hom_C_S(X,S) has a right adjoint. That adjoint is D_X/S(A). ULA relative duals are ULA and the bidual map is an equivalence; exterior products of ULA objects obey relative duality and ULA with the eligible hypotheses.
hypotheses: S is a small v-stack and X→S an object of C_S: compactifiable, representable in locally spatial diamonds, locally finite dim.trg.
A∈D_et(X,Λ).
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: ULA gives the relative internal-Hom and exceptional-base-change identities of IV.2.15/IV.2.19.
Construct evaluation/counit by f_!⊣f! and coevaluation on the diagonal; verify triangle identities using the displayed map.
Conversely the kernel adjunction forces overconvergence and compact direct-image constructibility through continuity, recovering both ULA clauses; transpose adjoints to get biduality.

nodes.title: ULA on Artin v-stacks
nodes.statement: For f:X→S of Artin v-stacks, assume there exists a surjective separated representable smooth chart g:U→X with U locally spatial and f∘g compactifiable of locally finite transcendence dimension. A∈D_et(X,Λ) is f-ULA iff g*A is (f∘g)-ULA. This is independent of g by common refinements and smooth source/base descent. Operations and relative-dual statements extend only when the operations in question have been constructed.
hypotheses: f:X→S is a map of Artin v-stacks.
There is a separated, cohomologically smooth surjection g:U→X from a locally spatial diamond, representable in locally spatial diamonds, with f∘g compactifiable of locally finite dim.trg.
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Choose a chart satisfying the composition hypothesis, which is stronger than merely being an Artin atlas.
Compare two choices on U×X V by smooth locality and v-local base descent.
Descend the resulting property, retaining explicit operation-existence conditions.
acceptance: The definition agrees with diamond ULA when X,S are diamonds.
A map of Artin stacks with no eligible composite chart is not asserted to satisfy this definition.

nodes.title: Relative adjoints and ULA calculus
nodes.statement: In C_S, a p₂-ULA kernel A:X→Y is a left adjoint when Y→S is proper; its right adjoint is the switched relative dual. ULA is preserved by relative duality with biduality, exterior products and eligible composition g*A⊗B, with the corresponding dual formulas. If f is a retract over S of eligible g and Λ is g-ULA, then Λ is f-ULA. For proper quasi-pro-étale g:Y→X and eligible f:X→S, A is (fg)-ULA iff Rg*A is f-ULA. ULA base change gives f*Rg*A⊗B≃Rĝ*(f′*A⊗ĝ*B) for f-ULA B and arbitrary base map g.
hypotheses: S is a small v-stack; all maps are compactifiable, representable in locally spatial diamonds, with locally finite dim.trg.
In IV.2.24, Y→S is proper.
In IV.2.28, g is proper and quasi-pro-étale and the spaces are locally spatial diamonds.
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Construct adjunction maps from the relative identity section, using properness to replace ! by *.
Compose kernel adjunctions and use the opposite symmetry for duality, exterior products and retracts.
Proper quasi-pro-étale pushforward on the product is conservative by profinite stalks; apply the dualizability criterion, then the tensor-Hom formula for arbitrary base change.
acceptance: The relative-kernel assertion retains properness of Y/S.
The retract assertion concerns the constant sheaf, not arbitrary retracting sheaves.

Corollary IV.2.25: duals and exterior products. Proposition IV.2.26: g*A⊗B is (f∘g)-ULA with the dual formula. Corollary IV.2.27: ULA of Λ passes to retracts. Proposition IV.2.28: for g proper and quasi-pro-étale, A is (f∘g)-ULA iff Rg_*A is f-ULA. Corollary IV.2.29: ULA base change.

nodes.title: Condensed affine points
nodes.statement: For a base ring R, affine R-scheme Spec B and condensed commutative R-algebra A, define its condensed points by sheafifying the functor S↦Hom_Ralg(B,A(S)); in fact it is already a sheaf because Hom preserves limits. This uses the pinned sheaf site and genuine representability; an arbitrary accessible functor on R-algebras need not preserve products or sheaf descent (the inherited source error E10). For finite presentation, polynomial points and equations give the product/equalizer presentation and filtered-colimit accessibility.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring, B a commutative R-algebra and A a condensed commutative R-algebra.
The scheme is affine; no statement is made for arbitrary accessible functors.
proofSteps: Evaluate Hom_Ralg(B,−) sectionwise; arbitrary limits are preserved, so the sheaf equalizers and products hold.
Use the universal polynomial ring for affine-space points and relations for closed equations.
Finite presentation gives filtered-colimit compatibility; no implication from accessibility alone to the sheaf condition is used.
acceptance: Affine n-space gives A^n including n=0.
The inherited E10 counterexample is excluded by representability.

nodes.title: Breen–Deligne resolution
nodes.statement: There is a functorial resolution of every abelian group A by terms finite direct sums of Z[A^r], with augmentation Z[A]→A. Its differentials are universal finite integral combinations of maps induced by integer matrices, so it applies after sheafification in any topos. The natural scalar n action and the action induced by A→A, a↦na, are chain homotopic. Applied to condensed groups it gives the finite-power RHom spectral sequence used for solidification and sheaf solidity.
hypotheses: A is an abelian group, or an abelian group object of a topos by functoriality.
proofSteps: Prove pseudo-coherence of the identity functor on finitely generated lattices by iterated bar constructions and the stable-range Eilenberg–Mac Lane homology input recorded as a gap.
Resolve it by finite sums of free finite-power functors; the differentials are universal matrix combinations.
Extend through simplicial free resolutions and exact sheafification; functorial comparison yields the scalar homotopy of 4.17.
acceptance: The first terms encode addition and associativity: Z[A²] and Z[A³]⊕Z[A²].
Finite multiplicities in each degree are essential; arbitrary infinite free resolutions do not give the same compactness argument.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.5 and Remarks 4.6–4.7, pp.25–26; Appendix to Lecture IV: Theorem 4.10, Proposition 4.12, Theorem 4.14, Lemma 4.15, Theorem 4.16, Proposition 4.17, pp.29–32
sources.match: Theorem 4.5, restated and proved in the appendix as Theorem 4.10, gives a functorial resolution of an abelian group A by finite direct sums of Z[A^r]; Remark 4.7 notes it applies in any topos; the appendix proves it through pseudocoherence of the identity functor on lattices (Definition 4.11, Proposition 4.12, Theorem 4.14, Lemma 4.15) from the Eilenberg–Mac Lane computation of Theorem 4.16; Proposition 4.17 gives the functorial homotopy between multiplication by n and the map induced by n on A.

nodes.title: Quasicompactness of closed affine points
nodes.statement: For a quasiseparated condensed commutative ring A and a closed immersion X→A_R^n, X(A)→A^n is a quasicompact monomorphism, hence X(A) is quasiseparated. With finitely many equations this is a pullback of a point along A^n→A^r. For arbitrarily many equations, on every profinite source the simultaneous zero set is an intersection of closed compact subsets, hence remains compact and represents the fibre. The finiteness of n is retained.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring and X→A^n_R a closed immersion, with n finite.
A is a quasi-separated condensed R-algebra.
proofSteps: For finitely many equations use quasiseparatedness to make the zero fibre over a profinite source compact Hausdorff.
For arbitrary relations, intersect their closed zero fibres in that compact source; the intersection is again profinite and represents simultaneous vanishing.
The resulting relative qc monomorphism gives quasiseparatedness by the subobject criterion. The printed A-valued multi-equation notation is interpreted as A^r.
acceptance: A single equation uses a map to A, whereas r equations use A^r.
Quasicompactness of the morphism does not assert A^n itself is quasicompact.

sources.locator: Appendix A, Lemma A.8 and proof, p.91
sources.match: Lemma A.8 states that for a closed immersion X→A^n_R and a quasi-separated condensed R-algebra A, X(A)→A^n is a quasi-compact injection; the printed proof takes finitely many equations and writes their joint value in A (source issue E1).

nodes.title: Completed ULA and solid kernel duality
nodes.statement: For Λ=lim_n Z/n over a specified system of integers prime to p and eligible f:X→S, D_ULA(X/S,Λ) consists of derived-complete compatible torsion reductions that are f-ULA. Write A∨=RHom_solid(A,Λ). For A of bounded Tor amplitude, B∈D_et(X,Z/n), Proposition VII.5.2 gives f♯(D_X/S(A)∨⊗solid B)≃Rf_!(A_n⊗ᴸ B). If f is proper, representable in spatial diamonds and of finite transcendence dimension, then for every solid B, f♯(D_X/S(A)∨⊗solid B)≃Rf*RHom_solid(A∨,B). On proper spatial finite-dimensional finite-Tor kernels, A↦A∨ reverses 2-morphisms and transports !-convolution to ♯-convolution. In particular A∨ is right adjoint to D_X/S(A)∨ in the solid kernel category. Both solid duals and the properness hypothesis in the second formula are essential.
hypotheses: Λ is a quotient of Zhat^p of the form lim_n Z/n over a set of integers prime to p.

f:X→S is a compactifiable map of small v-stacks, representable in locally spatial diamonds, with locally finite dim.trg; proper and representable in spatial diamonds with dim.trg finite for VII.5.3–VII.5.4.
A∈D_ULA(X/S,Λ) has bounded Tor-amplitude.
proofSteps: Form the enhanced inverse limit of the torsion ULA subcategories, importing derived completion and torsion Verdier duality; compare A∨ with lim_n A_n∨.

For VII.5.2 use the torsion tensor-Hom identity IV.2.19 and solid biduality VII.4.1 to construct the comparison by adjunction. Reduce to qc separated étale generator B=j!Λ after spatial descent. The cone is bounded above with finitely presented solid cohomology, so detection by constructible torsion test objects makes it zero.

For proper f in VII.5.3, the identity of A gives the diagonal coevaluation through IV.2.23. Finite cohomological dimension and bounded Tor amplitude give sum preservation; reduce B to finitely presented solid objects, then to their constructible torsion inverse-limit presentations and VII.5.2.

For VII.5.4 compare tensor and proper pushforward under A↦A∨ using VII.4.2–4.3. Reversing the 2-morphism direction converts the torsion ULA right-adjoint statement into the stated solid-kernel adjunction.
acceptance: For proper f=id the formula is the ordinary tensor-Hom identity for the solid duals of a perfect complex; deleting either dual changes the formula.
For a nonproper eligible f only the VII.5.2 torsion-target formula is asserted, without replacing Rf_! by Rf*.
Finite Tor amplitude, spatial representability and finite dimension are retained in the proper kernel transport.

sources.locator: VII.5, Propositions VII.5.2–VII.5.3; Corollary VII.5.4, pp.264–268
sources.match: Section VII.5 defines D_ULA(X/S,Λ) for Λ a limit of Z/n. Proposition VII.5.2: for A of bounded Tor-amplitude and B étale torsion, f_♮(D_{X/S}(A)∨⊗B)≅Rf_!(A_n⊗B); its proof uses Proposition VII.4.1 and Proposition IV.2.19. Proposition VII.5.3: for f proper, f_♮(D_{X/S}(A)∨⊗−)≅Rf_*RHom(A∨,−). Corollary VII.5.4: A∨ is right adjoint to D_{X/S}(A)∨ in the solid kernel 2-category, via the embedding of proper finite-Tor kernels given by VII.4.2–VII.4.3.

nodes.title: Cohomology of compact condensed spaces
nodes.statement: For compact Hausdorff S, condensed cohomology with discrete integer coefficients agrees with ordinary sheaf/Čech cohomology. Profinite S has H^i(S,Z)=0 for i>0. For the topological condensed reals, H^i(S,R)=0 for i>0 and H⁰=C(S,R). A profinite hypercover computes the latter by the augmented complex 0→C(S,R)→C(S0,R)→C(S1,R)→⋯; for i≥0, a cocycle in C(S_i,R) admits a primitive in the preceding augmented term (C(S,R) when i=0) of norm at most (1+ε) times its norm for each ε>0.
hypotheses: S is a compact Hausdorff space.
R is the condensed group of the topological reals.
proofSteps: For profinite sets approximate hypercovers by finite split covers; integer cochains are filtered colimits of exact finite complexes.
Compare the compact-Hausdorff and topological sites on stalks, using cofinal closed neighbourhoods and hypercovers.
For real cochains lift finite-level primitives with norm control, complete by a convergent correction series, and glue fibrewise primitives by Tietze extension and a finite partition of unity.
acceptance: Integer cohomology of a profinite set is concentrated in degree zero.
The norm-controlled real statement uses the topological real group, not discrete R.

sources.match: Theorem 3.2 identifies condensed cohomology of a compact Hausdorff space with integer coefficients with sheaf cohomology, with vanishing in positive degrees on profinite sets; Theorem 3.3 gives H^i(S,R)=0 for i>0, H⁰=C(S,R), and the quantitative exactness of the augmented complex of a profinite hypercover with primitives of norm at most (1+ε) times the norm.

nodes.title: Epimorphisms and quasiseparated colimits
nodes.statement: For a profinite condensed set S, evaluation at S commutes with filtered colimits because compact Hom and finite sheaf limits do. A condensed-set morphism surjective as a sheaf is an effective epimorphism. Filtered colimits of qcqs condensed sets along injections with quasicompact transition maps are quasiseparated. For quasiseparated X and profinite S, a morphism S→X is determined by its values on points; quasiseparated subobjects retain this point-detection property.
hypotheses: In A.5 the diagram is filtered, its objects are quasi-compact and quasi-separated and its transition maps are quasi-compact injections.
In A.7 the target is quasi-separated and the source profinite.
proofSteps: At a fixed regular cutoff, the profinite-site sheaf condition uses finite products and finite equalizers, which commute with filtered colimits. Transport this statement to the pinned CompHaus presentation through the recorded cutoff/site-comparison interface.

Apply sheaf descent for effective epimorphisms. For X=colim_i X_i and profinite T→X×X, evaluation/finite-product commutation first gives a common stage i through which T→X×X factors. Since X_i→X is a monomorphism, T×(X×X)X≃T×(X_i×X_i)X_i; quasi-separatedness of X_i makes this fibre quasicompact. Do not choose an arbitrary stage or assert X_i→X is quasicompact without proof.
On profinite pullbacks the equalizer is compact Hausdorff and closed; agreement on all points forces the maps to coincide.
acceptance: The transition hypotheses are retained in the filtered-union assertion.
Point detection is not asserted for arbitrary condensed sets.

sources.match: Lemma A.1: profinite sets are compact objects of condensed sets. Lemma A.2: surjections are effective epimorphisms. Lemma A.5: a filtered colimit of qcqs condensed sets along quasi-compact injections is quasi-separated. Lemma A.6: subobjects of quasi-separated condensed sets are quasi-separated. Lemma A.7: a map from a profinite set to a quasi-separated condensed set is determined by the map on underlying sets.

nodes.title: Derived Hom against reals and tori
nodes.statement: For A a product of copies of R/Z over any set, RHom(A,R)=0 in condensed groups; the source’s argument uses only that A is a compact Hausdorff abelian group, and gives the same vanishing for every such A. For a discrete abelian group M and a set I, RHom(product_I(R/Z),M)≃directSum_I M[-1]. In particular RHom(R,Z)=0 and RHom(product_I Z,Z)≃directSum_I Z, via 0→product Z→product R→product(R/Z)→0. These are condensed derived Hom statements, not ordinary abstract-group Hom computations.
hypotheses: A is a product of copies of R/Z over an arbitrary set (for the vanishing into R, any compact Hausdorff abelian group, by the same proof).
M is a discrete abelian group.
proofSteps: Apply the finite-power Breen–Deligne spectral sequence to identify the required derived Hom calculations with cohomology of compact powers.
For torus/discrete coefficients use homotopy invariance and cofiltered continuity of compact-Hausdorff Čech cohomology; that precise topological input is recorded as a gap.

For compact-to-real Hom compare multiplication by two with its functorial action, and sum the norm-controlled null-homotopy as a convergent geometric series; apply the product exact sequence for integer products.
acceptance: An abstract additive map R→R does not compute this condensed derived Hom.
The one-circle computation gives M[-1] with the stated shift.

sources.locator: Theorem 4.3, p.25, with its proof, pp.26–27; Corollary 4.8, p.26; proof of Proposition 5.7, p.35
sources.match: Theorem 4.3 states, for A a product of circles over any index set: RHom(A,M) is the direct sum of M[−1] for discrete M, and RHom(A,R)=0; its proof shows RHom(R,M)=0 for discrete M, and the proof of (ii) uses only that the powers of A are compact. Corollary 4.8 is the spectral sequence from the Breen–Deligne resolution. The proof of Proposition 5.7 deduces RHom of a product of copies of Z into Z.

nodes.title: Solid embedding of constructible coefficients
nodes.statement: For the analytification diamond X of a separated finite-type C-scheme over an algebraically closed nonarchimedean C and ell≠p, algebraic Verdier duality followed by solid duality yields a fully faithful covariant embedding D_c^b(X_alg,Z_ell)→D_ULA(X/Spa C,Z_ell)→D_solid(X,Z_ell). Its image consists of compact bounded objects with finitely presented solid cohomology, so it extends to Ind D_c^b(X_alg,Z_ell). The map sends i_*Z_ell at a C-point to i♯Z_ell and intertwines algebraic exceptional pullback with solid ordinary pullback. Thus the inverse limit of these scheme categories over finite-type charts X_alg→Y, with exceptional transition maps, embeds into D_solid(Y◇,Z_ell) as in Example VII.5.1(b), using separated charts and descent. Torsion analogues require finite Tor amplitude over Z/ell^m for the compact-image/Ind assertion; arbitrary bounded constructible torsion complexes are not asserted compact.
hypotheses: C is a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field and ell≠p.
X is the analytification of a separated scheme of finite type over C.
proofSteps: Import constructible Verdier biduality and exchange on the separated scheme charts. Use the algebraic/analytic ULA comparison and the coefficient-limit owner to form the compatible integral system; over Spa C every constructible system in this bounded range is ULA.

Compose Verdier duality and the fully faithful solid dual. The constructible Z_ell complexes have bounded Tor amplitude; the solid dual image is bounded with finitely presented cohomology and is compact by the source construction, giving the fully faithful Ind extension.

For a closed C-point, duality transforms i_*Z_ell into i♯Z_ell. For a scheme map f, use D_X′/S(Rf!A)∨≃(f*D_X/S(A))∨≃f*(D_X/S(A)∨). This gives the chartwise exceptional-to-ordinary transition comparison; form the enhanced inverse limit over charts to obtain the stack embedding.
acceptance: A C-point sends a perfect Z_ell complex to its expected covariant double-dual image.
A point-supported i_*Z_ell maps to i♯Z_ell, retaining the distinction from the naive solid inclusion.
Over Z/ell², the bounded complex Z/ell has infinite Tor amplitude and is excluded from a claim that all bounded constructible torsion objects have compact image.

sources.match: Example VII.5.1: for X the analytification of a variety over an algebraically closed C, every constructible complex is ULA over Spa C, giving a fully faithful embedding of D^b_c(X_alg,Z_ell) in the solid category that lands in compact objects and extends to the Ind-category; it sends i_*Z_ell at a point to i_♮Z_ell, intertwines Rf^! with solid pullback, and so embeds the limit over finite-type schemes over a stack with Rf^! transition maps.

nodes.title: Solid tensor and internal Hom
nodes.statement: There is a unique closed symmetric monoidal tensor on SolidAb making L symmetric monoidal, and a compatible colimit-preserving derived solid tensor on D(SolidAb). The internal derived Hom is characterized by the tensor-Hom adjunction and maps into the ambient condensed derived Hom. Integer products satisfy (product_I Z)⊗solid(product_J Z)≃product_(I×J) Z, including the derived comparison. The unit is discrete Z; derived solidification is monoidal.
hypotheses: Solid abelian groups in the sense of the pinned predicate over the integers.
The derived statements use the common enhancement.
proofSteps: The solidification kernel is a tensor ideal, so the reflection transports the ambient monoidal structure.
Compute the tensor on integer-product projective generators and extend by colimits and resolutions.
Construct the closed Hom by the common adjoint formalism and identify its ambient value on the generators.
acceptance: The product formula uses solid tensor, not an ordinary algebraic tensor of underlying groups.
Z_p⊗solid Z_ell=0 for distinct primes, while Z_p⊗solid Z_p≃Z_p.

nodes.title: Correct solidity for general discrete rings
nodes.statement: For an ordinary ring R and condensed R-module M, define corrected solidity by requiring that for every ring map Z[X]→R, restriction of M to Z[X] satisfies the pinned finite-type integer-algebra Hom-inversion predicate. Equivalently test every r∈R with X sent to r. For R finitely generated over Z it agrees with the finite-type predicate. It is not the naive all-R profiniteSolid Hom-inversion predicate, and it is not a definition of an analytic structure for arbitrary condensed rings.
hypotheses: R is a ring and M a condensed R-module.
The test is over all ring maps Z[X]→R, using the pinned predicate over Z[X].
proofSteps: Postcompose the actual module sheaf by the pinned restriction-of-scalars functor, which preserves the limits in the sheaf condition.
Apply the finite-type polynomial predicate for every ring map, as prescribed by the pinned TODO.
Use the finite-type analytic construction to compare the two predicates when R is finitely generated over Z; no such comparison is asserted for arbitrary R.
acceptance: Over Z this recovers the already pinned integer predicate.

nodes.title: Quasicompact and quasiseparated condensed sets

It is quasiseparated when its diagonal is quasicompact: for maps S,T→X from profinite sets, S×X T is quasicompact. A map is quasicompact when every pullback to a profinite set is quasicompact. These are site-theoretic definitions on the pinned CondensedSet, not replacements by properties of the abstract set X(point).

nodes.title: Solid geometric field-extension invariance
nodes.statement: For a small v-stack X and a solid Zhat^p-algebra Λ, solid pullback is fully faithful in each of three cases: (i) X is over an algebraically closed discrete field k of characteristic p and k′/k is an algebraically closed discrete extension; (ii) X is over such k and base change is to Spa(C,C⁺), with C/k complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean and C⁺ an open bounded valuation subring containing k; (iii) X is over Spa(C,C⁺), and base change is along a surjective map Spa(C′,C′⁺)→Spa(C,C⁺), with C′/C complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean and C′⁺ an open bounded valuation subring containing C⁺. The coefficient and site cutoffs must be compatible and large enough for these spaces.
hypotheses: X is a small v-stack.
Case (i): X over a discrete algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, k′/k discrete algebraically closed.
Case (ii): X over k, C/k complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean, C⁺ an open bounded valuation subring containing k.
Case (iii): X over Spa(C,C⁺), C′/C complete algebraically closed, C′⁺ containing C⁺, Spa(C′,C′⁺)→Spa(C,C⁺) surjective.
Λ is a solid Zhat^p-algebra; categories are formed at compatible, sufficiently large cutoffs.
proofSteps: Reduce coefficients to Zhat^p by restriction and use spatial-chart descent to test the adjunction unit. Postnikov truncations reduce to degree-zero finitely presented solid sheaves, which have cofiltered constructible torsion presentations.
For valued-field extension, commute the controlled cofiltered torsion systems with qcqs pushforward and apply ECD Theorem 19.5(iii), retaining the surjectivity and valuation-subring hypotheses.

For discrete-to-valued base change, work over the completed algebraic closure of k((t)) and use punctured-disc annuli and the torsion invariance proof of ECD Theorem 19.5(ii). Compatible cofiltered and filtered systems recover the solid unit.

For discrete algebraically closed extensions, choose compatible complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean extensions of the two fields and reduce to the preceding cases. This uses only generic diamond cohomology and solid operations, without the divisor or ULA applications.
acceptance: For every pair A,B, pullback induces an equivalence of mapping complexes; injectivity alone is insufficient.
The identity extension gives the identity pullback. The valued-field case keeps surjectivity of Spa(C′,C′⁺)→Spa(C,C⁺), rather than inferring it merely from the field inclusion.

sources.match: Proposition VII.2.6 states full faithfulness of solid pullback in three cases: an extension of discrete algebraically closed fields; base change from such a field to Spa(C,C⁺); and a surjective base change Spa(C′,C′⁺)→Spa(C,C⁺). Its proof reduces to ECD Theorem 19.5 through finitely presented solid sheaves and, in the second case, the annuli of the punctured disc.

nodes.title: Solid Drinfeld descent
nodes.statement: Fix an algebraically closed field k over F_q and the divisor-to-Weil map ψ:Div¹→[*/W_E]. For a small v-stack X over k and a solid Zhat^p-algebra Λ at compatible adequate cutoffs, ψ_X* : D_solid(X×[*/W_E],Λ)→D_solid(X×Div¹,Λ) is fully faithful. It is an equivalence if the separate geometric pullback D_solid(X,Λ)→D_solid(X×Spd Ē,Λ) is an equivalence, where Ē is the completed algebraic closure used in the Weil-torsor presentation. For each finite index set I, the corresponding product pullback ψ_X^I* is fully faithful.
hypotheses: k is an algebraically closed field over F_q; X is a small v-stack over k; I is a finite set.
Λ is a solid Zhat^p-algebra; categories are formed at compatible, sufficiently large cutoffs.
proofSteps: Use the existing divisor-to-Weil map and its continuous Weil-torsor presentation; do not replace W_E by its profinite completion.
Apply generic solid geometric field-extension invariance to the torsor charts, then descend the fully faithful unit. Essential surjectivity uses the separately stated geometric-pullback equivalence.
Iterate the single-factor comparison for finite I and retain the full-faithfulness conclusion of Corollary VII.2.8.
acceptance: Full faithfulness includes Hom isomorphisms, not merely faithfulness.
The finite-I assertion is not unrestricted essential surjectivity.

sources.match: Corollary VII.2.7 states that ψ_X* is fully faithful on solid categories and an equivalence when D_solid(X,Λ)→D_solid(X×Spd of the completed algebraic closure,Λ) is; it is deduced from Proposition VII.2.6 by descent along X→X×[*/W_E]. Corollary VII.2.8 is the finite-I version.

nodes.statement: Under the proper finite-dimensional spatial X and spatial S hypotheses of VII.2.9, let α:X×k S→X and C=α*A. If A is bounded below, or X→Spd k is cohomologically smooth, then Rβ_!+C=0=Rβ_!−C in solid coefficients. proofSteps: Base change to a geometric point over k((t)); in the smooth alternative establish finite cohomological dimension and reduce to bounded below.
Reduce on annuli to finitely presented solid sheaves and their cofiltered finite torsion presentations.

nodes.title: Solid sheaf structure and completion
nodes.statement: On spatial X solid Zhat-sheaves form an abelian full subcategory closed under all limits, colimits and extensions. Its finitely presented objects are exactly cofiltered limits of constructible torsion étale sheaves, forming their Pro-category; all solid sheaves form its Ind-category. Higher inverse limits of those torsion constructible systems vanish. Derived solidity is the derived Hom extension criterion; the derived inclusion is fully faithful and admits solidification with tensor-ideal kernel. Cutoffs supply the compatible presentable categories, without global presentability of the unrestricted site.
hypotheses: X is a spatial diamond (a diamond for VII.1.15).
Coefficients are Zhat.
proofSteps: On w-contractible charts cofiltered constructible torsion sheaves have exact inverse limits; use their compact representability.
Present free-solid chart objects as such limits; the finite-power resolution gives the closure and derived Hom criterion.
Apply the common derived reflection theorem at site-size cutoffs and verify compatibility between cutoffs; tensor annihilates its kernel.
acceptance: qcqs representability alone is not identified with solidity: VII.1.4 is a question.
Derived solidification is not asserted t-exact.

sources.locator: Theorem VII.1.3; Question VII.1.4; Proposition VII.1.6; Propositions VII.1.12–VII.1.15, pp.245–251
