Proposition VII.1.6: higher inverse limits of cofiltered systems of torsion constructible sheaves vanish. Propositions VII.1.12–VII.1.15: the derived extension criterion, the left adjoint, the tensor ideal and the left adjoint on the v-site of a diamond. Question VII.1.4 is left open by the source.

nodes.title: Solid sheaves on small v-stacks
nodes.statement: On spatial X and j:U→X a cofiltered limit of qcqs étale j_i, put j♯ Zhat=lim_i j_i! Zhat, with its tautological section on U. A pro-étale Zhat-sheaf F is solid when Hom(j♯ Zhat,F)→F(U) is an isomorphism for every such j. On a small v-stack solidity is this property after every spatial v-chart. D_solid(X,Zhat^p) is the full enhanced derived subcategory with solid cohomology; for an algebra object Λ it is the module category with solid underlying Zhat^p-complex. It is not the naive analytic Λ-solid category for arbitrary Λ.
hypotheses: X is a spatial diamond for the sheaf-level definition, a small v-stack in general.
Coefficients are Zhat, then a solid Zhat-algebra (a solid Zhat^p-algebra from VII.2 on).
proofSteps: Construct the chart free objects from qcqs étale inverse systems; finite-stage uniqueness makes them independent of presentation.
Impose the section-extension Hom criterion; check v-descent using the supplied quasi-pro-étale basis and Breen’s finite-power resolution.
Use the common enhancement for cohomological solidity and algebra-module objects, with compatible site-size cutoffs.
acceptance: On an algebraically closed geometric point this recovers the solid condensed coefficient category.
The unrestricted large D_solid need not be presentable at a fixed universe.

nodes.title: Solidification as a reflection
nodes.statement: The inclusion SolidAb→CondensedAb has a left adjoint L, the unique colimit-preserving extension of the pinned Z[S]→Z[S]_solid on the profinite compact-projective generators. The unit induces Hom(LA,B)≃Hom(A,iB) for every solid B; its counit is an isomorphism. The derived inclusion D(SolidAb)→D(CondensedAb) is fully faithful, with image the complexes having solid cohomology, and its left adjoint is the left derived solidification L^L. Derived solidification need not be concentrated in degree zero.
hypotheses: Solidity is the pinned predicate over the integers.
The derived statements use the common enhancement.
proofSteps: Apply the compact-projective reflection criterion verified in the abelian structure theorem.
Use the adjunction to characterize the unit and idempotence, and compare its profinite generator values with the pinned map.
Derive the reflection using projective resolutions and the common enhancement; cohomological solidity characterizes the fully faithful image.
acceptance: L fixes every solid group but is not the identity on all condensed groups.
The source’s derived examples prohibit claiming exactness/t-exactness of solidification.

sources.match: Theorem 5.8 gives the left adjoint of the inclusion of solid abelian groups as the unique colimit-preserving extension of Z[S]↦Z[S]_solid, and the derived statement: D(Solid)→D(Cond(Ab)) is fully faithful with image the complexes with solid cohomology and left adjoint the left derived solidification. nodes.title: Torsion embeddings into solid categories
nodes.statement: For Λ=Z/n with n prime to p, the naive D_et(X,Λ)→D_solid(X,Λ) is fully faithful, monoidal and pullback-compatible, with right adjoint R_Xet. It matches Rf* for qcqs f on bounded-below objects, or qcqs f of finite cohomological dimension. On overconvergent objects the solid dual A∨=RHom_solid(A,Λ) gives a fully faithful t-exact contravariant embedding with solid biduality and pullback compatibility. Its tensor comparison is an equivalence when one input has finite Tor amplitude. For proper spatial finite-dimensional f, (Rf*A)∨≃f♯A∨ on the overconvergent range.
hypotheses: Λ=Z/n with n prime to p for the dual embedding; Λ discrete with nΛ=0 for the naive one.
The dual embedding is on overconvergent objects; the tensor comparison needs finite Tor-amplitude of one factor.
In VII.4.3, f is proper, representable in spatial diamonds, with dim.trg finite.
proofSteps: Use the fully faithful sheaf-derived inclusion for the naive functor. Check tensor and pullback on qc separated étale j!Λ generators; construct R_Xet by the sheaf-category right adjoint, retaining the bounded-below or finite-cohomological-dimension pushforward range. This VII.4 argument does not assume ULA or the relative tensor-Hom criterion IV.2.19.
On strictly totally disconnected charts identify overconvergent torsion objects with an Ind-category of finite constructibles; solid duality realizes its Pro-category.
Use Breen’s resolution for biduality and the finite-Tor tensor comparison, then proper base change for the pushforward-dual identity.
acceptance: Naive and dual embeddings have different variance and convolution behavior.
No unrestricted finite-Tor-free tensor comparison is asserted.

sources.locator: VII.4 opening comparison; Propositions VII.4.1–VII.4.3, pp.261–264

VII.4.1 (naive embedding): D_et embeds fully faithfully and symmetric monoidally in the solid category, compatibly with pullback, with a right adjoint, and with pushforward in the stated ranges. Proposition VII.4.1: on overconvergent objects A↦A∨ is fully faithful, t-exact, pullback-compatible and bidual. Proposition VII.4.2: the tensor comparison for finite Tor-amplitude. Proposition VII.4.3: (Rf_*A)∨≅f_♮A∨ for f proper, representable in spatial diamonds, of finite dim.trg. None of these uses universal local acyclicity.

nodes.title: Z-solid analytification of schemes
nodes.statement: For a discrete commutative ring A, let Mod_Zsolid(A) be condensed A-modules whose underlying condensed integer group is solid. The affine analytic stack is AnSpec(A,Mod_Zsolid(A)); affine Zariski gluing defines X↦X_tilde for schemes. The associated module category is enhanced D(Mod_Zsolid(A)). The AnSpec and !-topology/gluing constructions are imported from AnalyticStacks AS.2–AS.3. This node specializes them to the Z-solid analytic structure; the comparison of regular-cutoff and light analytic coefficient models is an explicit interface gap.
hypotheses: A is a discrete commutative ring.
AnSpec and gluing are imported from AnalyticStacks; analytic rings from SolidAnalyticRings.
proofSteps: Form A-module objects whose integer restriction belongs to SolidAb; retain the discrete topology of A.
Apply the requested AnSpec and analytic Zariski descent from AS.2–AS.3 to the imported Z-solid analytic structure; do not construct a second generic analytic-stack category.
Glue the affine construction with the source’s analytic localization maps and compare the module categories on affine charts.

For lisse A,B define RHom_lis(A,B)=(RHom_solid(A,B))_lis and Rf_lis*B=(Rf*B)_lis; these are right adjoints to restricted tensor and pullback. No global presentability of D_solid is used.

Compare inclusion right adjoints for increasing cutoffs and glue them, with generator sections characterizing the kernel.

If Λ is killed by a power of ell, D_lis(X,Λ) is contained in the naive image of D_et(X,Λ). Equality requires a separated ell-smooth atlas U→X whose étale site has a basis of bounded ell-cohomological dimension. ell≠p; Λ=Z_ell⊗_(Z_ell,disc)Λ_disc for a discrete Z_ell-algebra Λ_disc (this includes Q_ell-algebras).

proofSteps: Evaluate relative-discrete scalar extension at the point, where evaluation is symmetric monoidal; reduce by sums to the free module.

Z is a cofiltered intersection of qcqs open neighbourhoods V with RΓ(V,F_ell)≅F_ell.

nodes.title: Sheaves and smooth representations
nodes.statement: For H locally pro-p and a ring Λ killed by an integer prime to p, there is a symmetric monoidal equivalence D_sm(H,Λ)≃D_et([*/H],Λ). Pullback along *→[*/H] is forgetting the action; structural pushforward is derived continuous invariants and internal RHom(−,Λ) is the imported derived smooth dual. The same category is obtained on [Spa C/H] for complete algebraically closed C/k. In particular D_et(*,Λ)=D(Λ). Smooth representation categories and their enhancement are imported from SR.
hypotheses: G is a locally pro-p group.
Λ is a ring killed by an integer n prime to p.
C is a complete algebraically closed nonarchimedean field over k.
proofSteps: Send an imported smooth module V to continuous equivariant functions on torsors; quotient-map v-descent proves the sheaf condition. This uses continuous v/pro-étale torsor descent, not the generally nonsmooth point map as a smooth atlas.
The geometric étale site is the site of discrete continuous H-sets; its sheaves recover V as colim_K F(H/K).
Reduce locally to pro-p groups, where prime-to-p continuous cohomology vanishes; left completeness extends the heart equivalence to unbounded categories. Compare duals by the tensor-Hom adjunction.

nodes.title: Compact generation of Bun_G coefficients

nodes.statement: For reductive G₁,G₂ over E, Bun_(G₁×G₂)=Bun_G₁×Bun_G₂. nodes.title: Torsion Verdier exchange and reflexivity
nodes.statement: For open j:V→U between open Bun_G substacks and every torsion A∈D_et(V,Λ), j!RHom(A,Λ)≃RHom(Rj*A,Λ). review.reason: Confirmed at the first paragraph of Appendix A.1, p.90. It takes an arbitrary accessible presheaf on commutative rings and calls its composite with a condensed ring a condensed set. sourceIssues.printed: The remark excludes cohomological smoothness of the point atlas for every infinite group, overlooking infinite discrete groups.
sourceIssues.correction: For nondiscrete locally profinite H an infinite compact open subgroup gives the distribution obstruction. Discrete H gives an étale, cohomologically smooth point map even when H is infinite.
sourceIssues.reason: Take H=π^Z, a closed infinite discrete subgroup of GL_1(E). The pullback of *→[*/H] is H→*, a disjoint union of identity maps, so it is separated étale of local dimension zero; the existing theorem that étale maps are cohomologically smooth applies. Its dualizing sheaf is constant F_ell on every discrete point. The source’s distribution argument obstructs infinite compact profinite neighbourhoods, not infinite discrete sets.

earlierReviews.reason: Confirmed at IV.1.10: the distribution obstruction applies to infinite compact open subgroups. The closed infinite discrete subgroup π^Z⊂E× has an étale point atlas, whose base change is a disjoint union of identities, so the finite-only parenthesis is false.

review.reason: Confirmed at Remark IV.1.10, p.110. The remark says the point of [*/G] is not a cohomologically smooth chart unless G is finite, because the exceptional pullback of Λ along G→* is the sheaf of distributions on G. For a discrete group, finite or not, G→* is a disjoint union of copies of the point, hence étale and cohomologically smooth, and the sheaf of distributions is the constant sheaf. The correct exception is discrete G; for example the subgroup generated by a uniformizer in E^×, which is closed in GL_1(E). The remark's point, that G(E) and its open subgroups do not give smooth charts, is unaffected.

review.reason: Confirmed at the proof of Lemma A.5, pp.89–90. The proof takes a profinite T with a map to X×X and then draws a diagram in which T maps to X_i×X_i, without choosing i so that the map factors; for an arbitrary i it does not.
